question: Does RackTrack show me CVEs or security advisories for my switch?
answer:
No. RackTrack does not list CVEs, severity badges, or vulnerability counts anywhere. Security-advisory reporting was removed from the product, and the server deliberately does not read the advisory rows the lookup engine still carries.

The closest thing you get is on the Firmware Check screen: after a successful check, tap "Show details" and look at "Release notes excerpts". If the vendor's own notes for the newer release listed security fixes, they appear there as a block titled "Security fixes in <version>", alongside "Bug fixes", "New features", "Known issues" and "Deprecations".

So: if you need a vulnerability assessment, use your vendor's advisory page or your own security tooling. RackTrack answers "is there a newer firmware and what changed", not "am I vulnerable".
rootCause: server/app.js maps the agent's FirmwareAdvice onto the /api/firmware contract and explicitly skips advice.advisories; the only security-flavoured output is the target release's security_fixes list rendered as a changelog section.

question: Where is the "Firmware Check" screen? I can't find it in the menu.
answer:
It is not in any menu. The Firmware Check page exists at the address /firmware, but there is no button or nav item that takes you there — the sidebar only has Home, Scan, Two racks, Profile (plus Console/Lab for the platform owner and Data Sources/Marketplace for admins), and the phone bottom bar only has HOME, SCAN, PROFILE.

What to use instead, and what you normally want:

1. Open the rack, then Switches, pick your switch, and use the Firmware tab on the card. That version is filled in for you from the scan or the CMDB.
2. If you really want the standalone screen, type /firmware onto the end of the app address. You will have to type Make / Vendor, Model and Current version by hand — it knows nothing about your rack.

You still have to be signed in either way.
rootCause: The /firmware route is registered in App.jsx and has a page title entry in DesktopShell, but no NavLink in the desktop sidebar links array or the mobile BottomNav items, so it is URL-only.

question: The Firmware tab says "No firmware version recorded" or "Add a model to check for updates" — why won't it check?
answer:
The check needs all three of vendor, model and current version. Whichever one is missing is what the message is telling you.

1. If it says "Add a model to check for updates.", go up to the top of the card and use "Enter make / model" (or "Add model" / "Add vendor") to fill in what the scan missed.
2. If it says "No firmware version recorded.", tap "Enter version" and type the version the switch is running, e.g. 1.0.6 Build 20210323. Press Save.
3. The check starts as soon as you save — you will see "Checking for updates…".
4. To change it later, use "Edit version" next to the Firmware heading.

Anything you type here lives in this browser only.

rootCause: loadDetails() sets firmwareStatus='skipped' unless displayVendor and lookupModel resolve, and again unless a cleaned version exists; POST /api/firmware itself 400s with 'vendor, model, and currentVersion are required'.

question: The check worked but "Release notes excerpts" shows 0 and says it couldn't extract anything. Is that a bug?
answer:
No — it means we had a version number for you but no usable text from the vendor's notes. The excerpts only appear when the vendor release we have on file actually carries fixes or features written down for that release.

What the screen does for you:

1. Tap "Show details" to see the section. The number next to "Release notes excerpts" is how many blocks we found — 0 is normal for most vendors.
2. If it says "Couldn't fetch release notes: …", the vendor page could not be read. If it says "Couldn't extract any changelog sections from the page.", the page was read but had nothing we could split up.
3. Use "Search release notes ↗" or "Open page ↗" underneath to go read the vendor's page yourself.

When excerpts do appear, they are grouped as Security fixes, Bug fixes, New features, Known issues and Deprecations for the newer version.
symptoms: Couldn't extract any changelog sections from the page
rootCause: changelog[] is synthesized only from the target release's security_fixes/bug_fixes/new_features/known_issues/deprecations arrays; when those are empty (the usual case for the live 'pointer tier' lookup, which never synthesizes bullets) the section falls back to the empty state plus search links.

an LLM, and we have neither for the long tail. Honest by design.

question: The Firmware Check screen says "Vendor list unavailable: …" under the Make / Vendor box.
answer:
Only the type-ahead list of vendor names failed to load. The check itself still works — you can type the vendor name in full and carry on.

1. Type the vendor exactly as the manufacturer writes it (Cisco, Juniper, Aruba) instead of picking from the list.
2. Fill in Model and Current version and tap "Check firmware" as normal.
3. If you want the list back, reload the page — the list is fetched once when the screen opens.
4. If it keeps failing for everyone, it is a server-side problem, not your phone: report it with the exact text after "Vendor list unavailable:".
symptoms: Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment.
rootCause: FirmwarePage fetches /api/specs/vendors once on mount; that endpoint shells out to pipeline.all_vendor --list-vendors, which reads Switch_Vendors_Websites.xlsx and is killed after PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS (90s). Failure only disables the suggestion list.

question: RackTrack read the wrong firmware version off my photo, or didn't read one at all. How do I fix it?
answer:
Type it in yourself — your typed value wins over anything the photo produced, and it is what gets used for the check.

1. Open the rack, then Switches, pick the switch, and go to the Firmware tab.
2. Tap "Enter version" (or "Edit version" if something is already there), type the version, and Save. The lookup re-runs immediately with your value.

Why it happens: the version is read off the chassis label in your photo, and only three shapes of version are recognised — Huawei-style (V200R010C00), Cisco NX-OS style (9.3(7)I7(7)), and ordinary dotted numbers (16.9.5). Anything printed differently, too small, glare-covered or at an angle simply comes back blank. A blank version is not an error, it just means nothing matched.

To get a better read next time: photograph the label straight on, fill the frame with the chassis, and avoid direct glare.
rootCause: pipeline/ocr_devices.py parses the version out of the OCR text with three fixed regexes and returns null on no match; SwitchCard's effectiveVersionRaw prefers sw.os_version but falls back to the per-switch localStorage override the user types.

question: The Switch Info pop-up has its own "Firmware Update" card — is that different from the Firmware tab on the switch card?
answer:
Same lookup, different source for your current version.

The "Firmware Update" card inside the Switch Info pop-up (opened from a scan result, header reads "Switch Info · live · <host> · <vendor>") takes the version straight off the switch over SSH — it parses "Firmware Version" / "Software Version" out of the device's own system output, cleans it up ("5.0.2 Build 20220909 Rel.75392" becomes "5.0.2") and then runs the same check.

Its wording is slightly different from the switch card: "Up to date", "Upgrade available", or "Could not determine latest version", with Current version / Latest version rows and a "Release notes" link. While it runs it says "Checking vendor site for newer firmware…"; if the SSH read gave no model or version it says "Need both model and firmware version to check for updates."; if the lookup failed it says "Could not check: …".

The Firmware tab on the switch card uses whatever the scan/CMDB recorded, or what you typed — it never talks to the switch.

Need both model and firmware version to check for updates
rootCause: ResultsPage's SwitchInfoModal parses firmware from the live SSH system-info output, runs cleanFirmwareVersion() on it and calls the same POST /api/firmware; it renders its own headline set independent of SwitchInformationPage's fwHeadline.

question: How current is the firmware data, and how often does it refresh?
answer:
There is no automatic refresh. Nothing in the server schedules a firmware or advisory update.

• The "latest version" values come from the lookup agent's SQLite cache at Agent/Agent_scrap/data/switches.db. That cache is only filled when someone runs the fetcher by hand: `python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py` (all public vendors), `… nvd` (CVE data from NIST NVD), `… kev` (CISA actively-exploited overlay). No cron job, timer or startup hook calls it.
• Dedicated public fetchers exist for exactly three vendors — MikroTik (RouterOS), Ubiquiti (UniFi OS) and NVIDIA (Cumulus Linux). Everything else relies on a best-effort live web pointer lookup with an 8.5-second deadline, cached on success.
• On the client, a firmware result is cached in memory for the browser tab, keyed by rack + vendor + model + version, with no expiry. Reload the page to force a fresh call.

So when you tell a customer a firmware answer is "current", it is only as current as the last manual fetcher run.
symptoms: how old is the firmware data
rootCause: Firmware/advisory ingestion is a manually-invoked script (Agent_scrap/scripts/fetch_firmware.py); server/app.js has no scheduler for it, and the client cache in scanPrefetch.js is a module-level Map with no TTL.

question: A switch shows "Upgrade available" but the Latest version we display is the same age or older than what the customer is running. Why?
answer:
Because upToDate is a literal string comparison, not a version comparison. The server does `String(agentLatest).trim() === String(currentVersion).trim()` — anything that is not byte-identical (16.12.1 vs 16.12.01, trailing build text, different case) evaluates to false and the UI paints "Upgrade available".

On top of that, the advisor deliberately surfaces its cached "latest" pointer even when the customer's version is newer: _synthetic_diff_from_latest() keeps releases_behind at 0 and returns the cached row anyway. So a stale or wrong cached pointer becomes a false "Upgrade available" rather than being suppressed.

When a customer reports this: confirm the two strings on the card, tell them the badge means "different from our cached value", and point them at the release-notes/vendor link. Do not tell them they are behind.
symptoms: says upgrade but we are newer
rootCause: firmwarePayloadFromAgent computes upToDate by exact trimmed string equality; the agent's _synthetic_diff_from_latest returns the cached vendor-level latest unconditionally with releases_behind=0.

question: Which vendors do we actually have firmware data for, and what does a customer see for the rest?
answer:
Three tiers:

1. Public fetchers exist for MikroTik (RouterOS), Ubiquiti (UniFi OS) and NVIDIA (Cumulus Linux) only. These are the only vendors with a real per-release changelog path.
2. Login-gated vendors — Cisco, Juniper, Arista, HPE Aruba, Dell, Fortinet, plus everything the vendor registry marks as gated (Huawei, H3C, Lenovo, Tejas, ZTE, NEC, Fujitsu, ALE, RUCKUS, Extreme, Ciena, Nokia). For these the advisor returns release_notes_gated and a portal URL, and the card shows "Check vendor portal" with a "Vendor portal ↗" link.
3. Everything else — a best-effort live web lookup (8.5-second deadline) that can only produce a version pointer, never a changelog. If that fails the advisor returns "No firmware data available for <vendor>" or "No NOS specified and no default known for <vendor>", and the card shows "Latest version unknown" with the explanatory line under it.

Nothing here is a supported/unsupported device list — it is purely about whether we can reach that vendor's release information.

question: How much can we trust the "Latest version" values the shipped agent database returns?
answer:
Very little — treat the shipped cache as demo-grade, not authoritative. Do not quote it to a customer as a firmware recommendation.

The firmware_versions table in Agent/Agent_scrap/data/switches.db currently holds 16 rows, all written by the generic 'firmware_fetchers' path, and several are clearly mis-scraped: HPE Aruba Networking is stored as version "802.3af" (a PoE standard) with a picclick.com listing as its release-notes URL; Cisco is stored as "16.2" pointing at a Nexus 9336C-FX2 model page; MikroTik as "25.6196C16" pointing at a product page; Netgear as "36.75ZM17". Every row also has nos set to the vendor's own name rather than a real network OS, and release_date is null on all but one.

Consequence: any customer whose vendor happens to be one of those 16 rows gets a bogus "Latest" and a false "Upgrade available", plus a junk "Release notes" link. Re-running the fetchers or curating the rows is the fix; there is no in-app override.

rootCause: The generic live/pointer fetcher regex-matches any 'version-like' token on a search-result page and upserts it into firmware_versions with source='firmware_fetchers'; nothing validates the match against the real vendor NOS, and the shipped DB was populated from those runs.

question: If we re-enabled CVE reporting tomorrow, would there be anything to show?
answer:
No. Two independent blockers.

1. The security_advisories table in the shipped Agent/Agent_scrap/data/switches.db has 0 rows, and 0 rows flagged actively_exploited. The NVD and CISA-KEV fetchers have never been run against it (`fetch_firmware.py nvd` / `… kev`).
2. Even with data, the join would miss: advisories are bucketed per (vendor, nos), but every firmware_versions row in the shipped DB has nos set to the vendor name ("Cisco|Cisco", "MikroTik|MikroTik"), so advisories_for_version() would query a NOS bucket that never matches an NVD row.

The schema and code are complete — severity is stored as CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW with a CVSS v3.1 base score, ranked CRITICAL=4 → LOW=1, with CISA KEV (actively_exploited) sorted above everything else regardless of CVSS. None of it reaches the API: server/app.js drops advice.advisories on the floor. Any restoration is a data-ingestion project, not a UI change.

question: "Couldn't check for updates right now" — what actually failed on the server?
answer:
The firmware endpoint shells out to the Python agent CLI and maps every failure to a single ok:false payload with an HTTP 404, which the switch card renders as the one generic line. The real cause is in the error string, which the Firmware Check page (unlike the switch card) prints verbatim in its red banner:

• "agent not installed at Agent/Agent_scrap" — Agent/Agent_scrap/cli.py is missing on that host. The agent is cloned separately and is not part of this repo checkout.
• "Agent lookup took too long." — the CLI exceeded AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 ms and was SIGKILLed.
• "Agent failed to start." — spawn error (wrong pythonCmd, missing interpreter).
• "Agent returned no parsable JSON." — the last stdout line was not JSON; last 500 chars of stderr are attached as _stderr for the server log only.
• "Agent failed to return a firmware response." — agent responded but without a usable advice object.

Also note FirmwarePage can surface "Backend returned a non-JSON response (HTTP <status>). Is the server running?" and "Request failed: <message>. Is the backend running on port 3001?" — those are client-side network failures, not agent failures.
symptoms: Couldn't check for updates right now
Is the backend running on port 3001
rootCause: runAgentCli() resolves a small set of fixed error strings; firmwarePayloadFromAgent passes them through as payload.error and the route replies 404 when ok is false. SwitchInformationPage collapses all of them to one generic status line; FirmwarePage prints the raw string.

question: Is pipeline/firmware_overrides.json still used for the "latest known firmware" values?
answer:
No. It is dead data. Nothing in the repo reads it.

The file's own header claims it is "Consulted before web scraping in pipeline.firmware_check" and calls itself "the authoritative source for the 'latest known firmware' badge", but there is no pipeline/firmware_check.py, and a repo-wide grep for firmware_overrides returns only the file itself. /api/firmware routes exclusively through the Agent_scrap CLI (`--firmware "<vendor> <model>" <version>`), which reads its own SQLite DB.

question: Are the firmware and vendor lookup endpoints authenticated?
answer:
No. POST /api/firmware, POST /api/specs and GET /api/specs/vendors are all registered without auth.requireAuth, unlike the rack/scan/CMDB routes next to them. The client sends a token via authFetch, but the server does not require one.

Why this matters: each of these calls spawns a fresh Python process. /api/firmware allows the agent CLI up to AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 ms; /api/specs/vendors allows the pipeline module up to PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000 ms. There is no per-caller rate limit on either. An unauthenticated caller can therefore hold open long-lived Python processes and drive outbound web scraping from our host.

Do not mention this to customers. Treat it as a hardening item: add requireAuth plus a rate limit before any public exposure of the API host.
rootCause: The spec/firmware routes were added without the auth.requireAuth middleware used elsewhere in app.js, while each handler shells out to a Python child process with a 60-90 second wall-clock budget and no throttling.

question: What exactly is a connection / data source in RackTrack, and what does "Active" mean?
answer:
A connection (the app calls them Data Sources) is one saved set of credentials for an external system RackTrack reads device and ticket data from — your CMDB/ITSM, NetBox, SolarWinds Orion, CA/DX Spectrum, or your own SQL or REST database.

Where to find it: the "Data Sources" item in the desktop sidebar, or Profile → Data Sources. The screen is titled "Data Sources" and explains: "Saved databases this app can pull data from. The active connection is what every screen uses while you're signed in. Switch any time — the data refreshes from the new source."

The screen has two sections:
• Active — one card showing the connection currently in use, with an "Active" badge.
• Other saved — every other connection you have saved, each with a "Use" button.

Key rules:
1. Exactly one connection is active at a time. Pressing "Use" on another one switches every screen over to it; the previous one is deactivated but not deleted. The database enforces this with a unique index (one active row per user).
2. There is no merging across sources — the active connection is the single source of truth for that session.
3. Saved connections belong to the account that created them. The server scopes every read and write to your user id, so no one else can see or use your saved connections.

Organization-wide credentials are a separate thing — see the "Organization integrations" panel in the Organization Console.

rootCause: Connection profiles are per-user rows in connection_profiles with a unique partial index allowing one is_active=1 row per user; the Data Sources page renders an Active card and an 'Other saved' list with a Use button that calls the activate route.

question: Which data sources can I connect, and exactly what do I have to type in for each one?
answer:
Six types are supported. The Type dropdown shows these labels, and the form changes to the fields that type needs:

• ServiceNow / CMDB — Instance ID (e.g. dev266363), Username, Password. All required. Hint on the form: "Use just the instance ID — the part before .service-now.com". Do not paste the full https://…service-now.com URL; the server builds the hostname itself from what you type.
• NetBox — Base URL (e.g. https://netbox.example.com) and API Token, both required. Hint: "API token from your NetBox user profile".
• SolarWinds Orion — Host (e.g. orion.example.com), Username, Password, all required. Hint: "SolarWinds Orion NPM / NCM server".
• CA / DX Spectrum — Base URL (e.g. https://spectrum.example.com:8443), Username, Password, all required. Hint: "Spectrum OneClick / REST endpoint".
• My own database (SQL) — a single Connection string, required. Placeholder: postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/dbname. Hint: "PostgreSQL or MySQL connection string".
• My own database (REST) — Base URL (e.g. https://cmdb.example.com/api), required, plus an optional API Token. Hint: "Generic REST endpoint that returns device / interface JSON".

Anything not on this list is rejected by the server with "unsupported profile type: <type>".

question: How do I add a new data source connection, step by step?

question: Saving a connection failed with a message like "servicenow profile requires {instance, user, password}" or "name, type, secret are required". What is wrong?
answer:
The server refused the save because a required field was empty. Fill in every field marked with * for the type you picked, then press save again.

The exact messages and what each one means:
• "name, type, secret are required" — the Name box was empty, or no credential field was filled in at all.
• "servicenow profile requires {instance, user, password}" — one of Instance ID, Username or Password is blank.
• "netbox profile requires {base_url, token}" — Base URL or API Token is blank.
• "orion profile requires {host, user, password}" — Host, Username or Password is blank.
• "spectrum profile requires {base_url, user, password}" — Base URL, Username or Password is blank.
• "generic_sql profile requires {connection_string}" — the Connection string is blank.
• "generic_rest profile requires {base_url}" — the Base URL is blank (the API Token is genuinely optional for this type).
• "unsupported profile type: <type>" — the type is not one of the six the server accepts. That only happens if the request did not come from the Data Sources form.

In the Organization Console panel the check happens in the browser first and reads "Fill in: <field labels>" before anything is sent.

Note: whitespace alone does not count as filled in on the org panel, and on the Data Sources form the browser also blocks submit while a required field is empty on a new connection.

question: I only wanted to change the password on an existing connection, but saving fails with "servicenow profile requires {instance, user, password}". Why?
answer:
Because when you type into any credential field on the edit form, the whole set of credential fields is sent — and the ones you left blank are sent as blank, which wipes the stored values and then fails validation.

Fix: when you edit credentials, re-enter every required field for that type, not just the one you are changing. For ServiceNow that means Instance ID, Username and Password together.

Steps:
1. Open Data Sources, tap the ⋯ menu on the connection, choose "Edit".
2. Either leave every credential field blank (the note on the form says "Leave the credential fields blank to keep what's already saved") and change only the Name — or fill in all of the starred fields.
3. Press "Save changes".

So there are exactly two safe edits: rename only (all credential fields blank), or replace the credentials in full.

question: Where can I see the password I saved for a connection, and why is the Type dropdown greyed out when I edit?
answer:
You cannot see a saved credential again — not in the app, and not through the API. That is deliberate: RackTrack stores the credentials encrypted and only ever returns the connection's name, type, active flag and timestamps. When you open "Edit connection" the credential boxes are always empty; the code never pre-loads them.

What that means in practice:
• Lost the password? RackTrack cannot tell you what it was. Get it from the source system and re-enter it (all required fields together).
• The Organization Console panel says the same thing: "They're stored encrypted and are never shown again — not even to you. To change one, just re-enter it."

The Type dropdown is disabled while editing, with the note "Type can't change after a connection is created." To move a connection to a different system, add a new connection of the right type (it becomes active on save) and then delete the old one.

question: How do I test that a connection actually works? I can't find a "Test connection" button.
answer:
There is no Test button — RackTrack has no test endpoint for connection profiles. How you verify depends on the type:

ServiceNow / CMDB: when it is the active connection, a button appears under the Active card: "Refresh data from this source". Pressing it runs a real poll against the instance you entered, so it is the closest thing to a test.
• While it runs: "Pulling fresh data from <name>…"
• Success: "✓ Pulled N incidents from <instance>"
• Failure: "Refresh failed: <error from the poller>"
Saving with "Save & use", or pressing "Use" on a saved ServiceNow connection, starts the same poll automatically.

Every other type (NetBox, SolarWinds Orion, CA/DX Spectrum, own SQL, own REST): the refresh button is not shown, and nothing is contacted at save time — the credentials are simply stored. You confirm them by opening a screen that reads from that source and seeing whether data appears.

So a connection saving successfully proves only that the fields were filled in, never that the host, username or password are correct.

question: I re-entered our CMDB credentials in Organization integrations and now the same integration is listed twice. Which one is being used?
answer:
The newest one is being used. The older row is kept but is no longer active — the panel simply lists every stored row for the organization, and each row displays "● Configured · encrypted" whether or not it is the one in use.

What happens when you press "+ Add integration" for a type you already have: the server marks the previous credential of that type inactive and inserts a new active one. Nothing is overwritten in place, so the old row stays in the list.

Fix: press "Remove" on the stale row (you will be asked "Remove the <type> integration for this organization?"). Removing it does not affect the newest one. If you are not sure which is which, remove them all and add the integration once more.

An organization can hold one active credential per type at the same time — for example a live ServiceNow and a live SQL source together — so seeing two rows of *different* types is normal.

question: Saving an organization integration returns "organization admin only" or "no organization is associated with your account". What now?
answer:
Two different refusals:

• "organization admin only" (403) — your account is not an organization admin (and not the platform owner). Members and site managers cannot set organization-wide credentials. Ask your organization admin to do it; they set it once and everyone's scans then use it.

• "no organization is associated with your account" (400) — your role is accepted but your account is not attached to any organization. This is what a platform-owner account hits, because an owner sits above organizations and has no organization of its own. The fix is to use an organization-admin account inside the organization you want to configure. That is also why the "Organization integrations" panel is not rendered for the owner.

Both checks run on the server, so they apply to any client, not just the console screen.

rootCause: requireOrgAdmin in connection_profiles_routes.js returns 403 for roles outside org_admin/owner and 400 when req.user.organization_id is missing, which is the platform owner's case; OrgConsolePage hides the panel for owners.

question: How do I stop using a data source, or delete one? Is there an off switch?
answer:
There is no off switch on the Data Sources screen — your options are switch or delete.

To switch: press "Use" on another saved connection. The one you were on stops being active immediately and stays saved.

To delete:
1. Tap the ⋯ menu on the connection's card.
2. Choose "Delete".
3. Confirm the prompt: Delete connection "<name>"?

Deleting is permanent — the stored credentials go with the row and cannot be recovered, so you will have to type them in again if you want that source back.

If you delete the active connection and have no other, the screen shows "No active connection." with the hint "Add a connection below to start pulling data from your CMDB", and CMDB-backed screens stop returning data until you add one.

(For organization-wide credentials, the equivalent is the "Remove" button in Organization integrations.)

question: The ports screen says "The switch refused the connection — is SSH enabled on it?" What do I do?
answer:
That message means the switch answered on the network but nothing accepted the connection — so the address is reachable, it just isn't listening for RackTrack.

Try these in order:
1. Check the address you typed is the switch's management IP, not a server, an access point, or your default gateway. RackTrack suggests the last address that worked for you, so if you overtyped it, try the suggestion.
2. Ask your network team whether SSH (rather than only Telnet or the web UI) is enabled on that switch. This is the most common cause — the switch is up, the SSH service is not running.
3. If the switch runs SSH on a non-standard port, RackTrack has to be told: registered switches carry their own SSH port and default to 22. A switch listening on a different port with nothing on 22 gives exactly this message. Ask your admin to correct the registered SSH port.
4. Retry once after any change. Don't hammer Retry — small managed switches allow very few SSH sessions.

question: "The switch rejected the saved credentials" — or it says the login was accepted but the session closed. How do I fix it?
answer:
Neither of these is something you can fix from the phone; the switch login RackTrack uses lives on the server. But which message you get tells your admin exactly what to change, so pass it on word for word.

• "The switch rejected the saved credentials." — the username or password RackTrack holds for this switch no longer matches the switch's local account (usually because the switch password was rotated). Ask whoever administers the RackTrack server to update the stored switch login.
• "The switch accepted the login but closed the session — the saved switch account may not have CLI access. Check the switch credentials." — the login is correct, but that account isn't allowed a CLI session. It needs an account with CLI/exec access on the switch.
• "The switch accepted the login but refused a CLI session — its concurrent-session limit is saturated by stuck sessions." — do NOT keep retrying; every attempt adds another stuck session. It has to be cleared on the switch itself (disable and re-enable SSH from the switch web UI, or reboot it), then one attempt will succeed.

If you typed the username and password yourself in the login box, re-open it and re-type them carefully first — a typo produces the same rejection.

accepted the login but closed the session
rootCause: friendlyProbeError maps auth/denied/permission errors and session-closed errors to those strings; the SSH runner's close handler distinguishes post-auth channel refusal (session cap) from a pre-auth close.

question: INTERNAL: how are connection-profile credentials stored, and what may I say about it to a customer?
answer:
Storage model (do not paste this section to customers):
• Credentials for every connection profile — personal and organization-wide — are serialised to JSON and sealed with AES-256-GCM before they touch the database. The row stores base64(iv|tag|ciphertext) in connection_profiles.secret_blob. Only name, type, is_active, organization_id and timestamps are queryable in cleartext.
• The key is 32 bytes of hex, taken from the SSH_CREDS_KEY environment variable if set, otherwise from server/.env.key (written 0600). The same key protects the SSH credential store — one key, one rotation surface. On first run with no key present the store generates one.
• Nothing decrypts on the client. Decryption happens only inside the server process, in getWithSecret / getActiveWithSecretForOrg, at the moment an outbound call is made.
• No route returns plaintext. Create, update, list and get all reply with metadata only, including for the admin who set the credential.

Handling rules for support staff:
• Never read out, copy, screenshot, relay or "confirm" a stored secret, to anyone, including the account owner or an org admin. There is no supported way to retrieve one and you must not invent one.
• Never ask a customer to send you a password, token or connection string in a ticket. If a credential must change, the customer re-enters it themselves in the app.
• Do not discuss key file locations, environment variable names, or database column names with customers.

Safe customer-facing phrasing: "Your credentials are encrypted before they are stored, they are never shown again — not even to you — and the app can't display them back. To change one, just re-enter it."
symptoms: Customer asks us to retrieve their stored password
rootCause: connection_profiles.js encrypts the secret JSON with the shared AES-256-GCM helper from ssh-creds.js and persists only the blob; all HTTP responses go through rowToMeta/orgRowToMeta, which omit secret_blob.

question: INTERNAL: every connection suddenly stopped working after a server change and the log shows decrypt failures. What happened?
answer:
The encryption key no longer matches the stored blobs. Symptoms and handling:

What you see:
• server log: "[connection_profiles] decrypt failed for profile <id>: …" or "[connection_profiles] org decrypt failed for profile <id>: …", after which the profile resolves to null and CMDB-backed endpoints behave as if no connection is configured.
• SSH credential store: "[ssh-creds] decrypt failed — ignoring env creds: …", after which the server behaves as if no switch credentials exist at all (polls are skipped, audits return the no-credentials error).
• Profiles still LIST normally — name, type and Active badge are unaffected, because only the blob fails. That is why it looks like "the app forgot our password" rather than an outage.

Causes, in likelihood order:
1. server/.env.key was not carried across a redeploy or was deleted. On the next start the connection-profile store silently generates a brand-new key, so every existing blob becomes undecryptable.
2. SSH_CREDS_KEY is set in the environment to a different key — the env var takes precedence over the file, so an old file on disk will not save you.
3. The key file content was truncated or reformatted; it must be exactly 64 hex characters, otherwise the loader throws "<path> must contain a 32-byte hex key (64 chars)".

Recovery:
• Restore the original key material (file or env var) from backup BEFORE restarting again, then restart the server. Nothing else is needed — the blobs are intact.
• If the key is genuinely lost, the secrets are unrecoverable by design. Every connection profile and every switch credential must be re-entered: profiles by their owners/org admins in the app, switch credentials on the server. Do not attempt any other recovery path and never ask a customer for their credentials over a support channel — direct them to re-enter in the app.
• The keying material is backed up separately from the blob for exactly this reason; the CLI's init command warns about it.
symptoms: must contain a 32-byte hex key (64 chars)
All connections stopped working after redeploy
Connections still listed but no data pulled
rootCause: Both stores decrypt with a key resolved from SSH_CREDS_KEY or server/.env.key; a missing/replaced key makes decrypt throw, and the code logs and degrades to null/empty credentials rather than failing loudly. connection_profiles.loadKey auto-generates a fresh key when the file is absent, permanently orphaning existing blobs.

question: INTERNAL: is "only admins can manage connections" a real security boundary?
answer:
Partly. Be precise when answering security questionnaires:

• Personal connection profiles (/api/connections/*) are protected by requireAuth only, then scoped to req.user.id. Any authenticated user — including a member — can create, list, update, activate and delete THEIR OWN profiles through the API. What they cannot do is see or touch anyone else's: every statement filters on user_id.
• The "admins only" part is client-side presentation: the /connections route is wrapped in AdminRoute (redirects non-org_admin/owner to /), and the sidebar link plus the Profile row are rendered only for org_admin/owner. Treat this as a UI affordance, not an authorization control.
• Organization-wide credentials (/api/org-connections/*) ARE server-enforced: requireOrgAdmin rejects any role outside org_admin/owner with 403 and requires an organization_id, and every query is scoped to that organization id.
• Credential resolution has no environment or file fallback: resolveCredsForType and resolveCredsForOrg return null when there is no matching active profile, so a missing profile degrades to "no data" rather than quietly using someone else's credentials.

So: cross-tenant exposure of connection credentials is server-enforced; the admin-only *screen* is not. If a customer asks whether a technician can store their own CMDB credentials, the honest answer is that the app does not offer them the screen.

Can a member create a connection profile
rootCause: router.use('/api/connections', requireAuth) has no role check and all queries filter by user_id, while /api/org-connections adds requireOrgAdmin; the admin gate on the /connections page comes from AdminRoute and DesktopShell's isAdmin conditional.

question: What is the Marketplace in RackTrack and what are all those tabs at the top?
answer:
The Marketplace is RackTrack's second-hand exchange for surplus network and data-centre gear. The header reads "Marketplace — Buy, sell and swap surplus network and data-center gear", and every screen in the section shares the same nav bar:

• Browse — everything currently for sale (or, with the toggle flipped, everything Wanted).
• My listings — the things you have posted, with Edit / Mark sold / Relist / Delete.
• Orders — your Buying and Selling tabs, each order's status, tracking and the message thread with the other side.
• Alerts — saved searches and the new listings that matched them.
• Dashboard — your own selling and buying numbers.
• Partners — connect eBay, Amazon or a Discord channel.

Top right there is a "List an item" button on every screen except the new-listing form itself, and a back arrow top left.

A listing is one of two kinds: For sale (you have gear) or Wanted (you need gear and sellers come to you). Everything is filed under one of ten categories — Cables, Switches, Routers, Racks, Optics / SFPs, Servers, PDUs, Firewalls, Patch panels, Other — and one of four conditions: New, Refurbished, Used, For parts.

The whole section is limited to organization admins and the RackTrack platform owner; other roles never see the link and are sent back to the home screen if they type the address.

question: How do I find a specific part in the Marketplace? My search isn't finding anything.
answer:
Search only looks at three things — the listing title, the vendor and the model — and it only ever shows listings that are still active. If a part number returns nothing, widen the search.

1. Open Browse.
2. Type into "Search by title, vendor or model…". It waits a moment after you stop typing before searching, so give it a beat.
3. Use the "All categories" dropdown to narrow to Switches, Optics / SFPs, and so on.
4. Use the For sale / Wanted toggle. "For sale" is what people are selling; "Wanted" is what people are looking for. They are separate lists — a part you cannot find under For sale will not appear under Wanted.
5. If you get "Nothing matches those filters", press "Clear filters" and try fewer words. Search matches whole fragments of text, so "WS-C3850" works but a typo or extra spaces will not.

Results come 24 to a page with Previous / Next at the bottom; Next is only live when there really is another page.

Still nothing? Scroll past the results to "Can't find it here?" and type the part number there — that opens the same search on eBay, Amazon, FS.com or Curvature in a new tab. Those are plain links out; RackTrack is not involved in anything you buy there.

question: My listing won't publish — it says "title is required" / "bad category" / "bad price".
answer:
Those are the form's own checks. Fix the named field and press Publish listing again — nothing was saved, so you will not create a duplicate.

• "Title is required." or "title is required" — the Title box is empty or only spaces. Type a real title (a vendor plus model is enough).
• "bad price" — the Price box has something that isn't a plain positive number. Remove currency symbols, commas and letters, or clear the box entirely to list it as "Make an offer".
• "bad category" / "bad condition" / "bad kind" — the value sent wasn't one RackTrack accepts. Reselect Category and Condition from the dropdowns rather than typing, then submit again. If it keeps happening, reload the page — a stale tab can send an old value.
• "Please wait for the image to finish uploading." — your photo is still going up. Wait for the caption under it to change from "Uploading…" to "Photo ready" and press Publish again.

question: The photo on my listing won't upload — "Only image files are accepted" or "Image must be 8 MB or smaller".
answer:
RackTrack only takes real image files, and only up to 8 MB each. Fix the file, then re-pick it.

1. On the New listing screen, under Photo, the box says which formats work: JPG · PNG · WebP · HEIC · up to 8 MB.
2. "Image must be 8 MB or smaller." — the picture is too big. Shoot it again at a lower resolution, or send it through your phone's own resize/share-as-smaller option, then pick it again.
3. "Only image files are accepted (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC)." or "Only jpg / png / webp / heic images are accepted" — the file isn't one of those types. Screenshots and camera photos are fine; PDFs, GIFs and files that have lost their file extension are not. If you saved the picture without an extension, rename it so it ends in .jpg or .png and pick it again.
4. If it says "Upload failed", tap Replace and try once more — the photo is uploaded separately from the listing, so a failure there doesn't lose anything you have typed.
5. Tap Remove to drop the photo entirely. A photo is optional — the form only says listings with one sell faster.

Don't press Publish while the caption still reads "Uploading…" — the form will stop you and ask you to wait.

answer:
Buy now only appears when all three of these are true: the listing is still active, it is a For sale listing (not a Wanted request), and the seller set a price.

• "listing is not active" — somebody bought it, the seller marked it sold, or it was withdrawn while you had the page open. Go back to Browse and search again; sold and closed listings drop out of Browse.

question: What do the order statuses mean, and how do I mark an order shipped or cancel it?
answer:
Open Orders and pick Buying (things you bought) or Selling (things you sold). Each order shows one status pill:

• Pending — the order exists but payment has not been confirmed yet.
• Paid — payment is confirmed; the seller can ship.
• Shipped — the seller has sent it, usually with a carrier and tracking number.
• Completed — closed out for both sides.
• Cancelled — called off; the pill shows red.

What you can do, and when:

1. Ship it (seller only, order must be Paid). Open the order, fill in Carrier (UPS, USPS, FedEx…) and Tracking number under "Ship this order", then press "Mark shipped". The tracking number then shows on the order for the buyer.
2. Complete it (either side, order must be Shipped). Press "Mark completed", then confirm "Yes, complete" — the prompt warns it closes the order for both sides.
3. Cancel it (either side, order must be Pending or Paid). Press "Cancel order", then "Yes, cancel". It cannot be undone.

If you see "cannot cancel at this stage" the order has already shipped or closed — you can no longer cancel it; message the other party instead. "invalid status transition" means the step you asked for isn't allowed from where the order is now (for example, only the seller can mark something shipped).

question: How do I message the buyer or seller about an order, and why does the Orders tab have a number on it?
answer:
Every order has its own message thread, and that number is how many messages you haven't read yet.

1. Open Orders and tap the order. Scroll to Messages — it says who you're talking to ("with @<username>").
2. Type in the "Type a message…" box and press Enter, or tap the send arrow. Shift+Enter does not send.
3. Keep a message under 2000 characters — a longer one is refused with "message too long" and nothing is sent. Split it into two.
4. An empty message is refused with "message body required".
5. The thread refreshes itself about every half a minute while the order is open, so you'll see replies without reloading.
6. Simply opening the order marks the other person's messages as read — that is what clears the badge on the Orders tab. The badge shows "99+" once you're past ninety-nine.

Messages live on the order, so there is no way to message someone about a listing you haven't bought. For a listing with no price, contact the seller by the @username shown on the listing instead.

If you get "not your order", you are signed in as someone who is neither the buyer nor the seller on that order — check which account you're using.

rootCause: POST /api/marketplace/orders/:id/messages rejects an empty body and anything over 2000 chars; GET /api/marketplace/orders/:id marks the counterparty's messages read as a side effect; MarketplaceShell polls /orders/unread-count and /alerts/unread-count once per auth state and caps the badge at 99+.

question: How do Marketplace alerts work? I saved a search but I'm not getting any matches.
answer:
A saved search is a standing watch: when someone posts a NEW listing that fits it, a match appears under Alerts. It does not look backwards, so an empty Matches list usually just means nothing new has been posted yet.

To set one up:
1. Open Alerts, then "New search" (or "Save a search" if you have none yet).
2. Give it a Label — required, it's the name you'll see on each match ("e.g. Cisco switch under $2k").
3. Optionally add a Keyword, a Category, a Max price, and choose For sale or Wanted.
4. Press "Save search".

Why a search may never fire:
• It only checks listings created after you saved it — existing listings are never matched retroactively.
• Every filter you set must match. A Keyword only matches against the title, vendor or model. A Category set to Switches will ignore a switch someone filed under Other.
• Listing kind must match. A "For sale" search never matches a Wanted post.
• A Max price excludes anything priced above it. Listings with no price ("Make an offer") still come through.
• You are never alerted about your own listings.

Housekeeping: you can keep up to 20 saved searches — the 21st is refused with "max 20 saved searches". Alerts show the 50 most recent. "Mark all read" clears the badge; the small × on a row dismisses one match; deleting a saved search ("Stop alerts and delete?") also removes its matches.
rootCause: matchAlerts() runs only inside the POST /api/marketplace/listings response wrapper, so it evaluates saved searches against newly inserted rows only; it skips the listing's own owner, requires kind and (if set) category equality, a substring hit on title+vendor+model, and max_price_cents >= price. Saved searches are capped at 20 per user; GET /alerts is LIMIT 50; alerts cascade-delete with their saved search.

question: My listing disappeared from Browse and now shows "closed" — I didn't touch it.
answer:
Listings retire themselves after about three months. Anything still active 90 days after it was posted is automatically set to closed, which takes it off Browse but leaves it in your My listings with a grey "closed" pill.

To put it back:
1. Open My listings.
2. Find the listing — closed ones stay in this list; they only vanish from public Browse.
3. Press "Relist". It goes back to active immediately and reappears in Browse.
4. If the gear is gone, press Delete instead, then "Yes, delete".

Other reasons a listing can leave Browse:
• It says "sold" — either you pressed "Mark sold", or somebody bought the last one, which marks it sold automatically.
• The RackTrack platform owner hid it after it was reported. In that case it also shows as closed, and pressing Relist without fixing the reason will just get it hidden again — ask your platform owner what was wrong with it first.

The Dashboard's "Closed" tile is labelled "Expired or withdrawn", which covers both of these.

question: What do the numbers on the Marketplace Dashboard mean, and why is my revenue zero when I've sold things?
answer:
The Dashboard ("Seller dashboard — Listings, sales and purchases") is scoped to the signed-in account only, not to the whole organization, and Revenue counts completed orders only.

The three groups:
• Listings — Total, Active, Sold, Closed (Closed is captioned "Expired or withdrawn").
• Sales — Revenue, with "From N completed orders" underneath; plus Orders (all orders where you are the seller), Completed, and Pending, captioned "Awaiting shipment".
• Purchases — Spent, "Across N orders", plus your order count as a buyer.

Why Revenue can read zero:
1. Revenue only totals orders whose status is Completed. An order sitting at Paid or Shipped counts under Pending, not Revenue.
2. Fix it by closing out the finished orders: Orders → Selling → open the order → "Mark completed" → "Yes, complete". Only orders that are already Shipped can be completed.
3. Pending counts orders at Paid or Shipped — that number is your to-ship / to-close queue, not unpaid orders.

Everything here is per-user. If your organization has several admins selling, each sees only their own figures — there is no combined org view. "Recent listings" below shows your last ten, and "View all" jumps to My listings.

question: INTERNAL: A buyer says they paid but the order is still Pending — how does Marketplace payment actually work?
answer:
Marketplace payments are env-gated on the server, and the order's initial status depends entirely on whether Stripe is wired up on that deployment.

Two modes:
• STRIPE_SECRET_KEY unset (or the stripe package fails to load): no payment is taken at all. POST /api/marketplace/orders writes the order straight in as 'paid' — the code comments this as "offline payment assumed". The checkout button reads "Complete purchase — …". Treat every such order as an IOU settled outside RackTrack. Never tell a customer RackTrack charged them.
• STRIPE_SECRET_KEY set: the order is written as 'pending', a Stripe Checkout Session is created with the order id in metadata, and the client is redirected to session.url. The order only flips to 'paid' when POST /api/marketplace/stripe/webhook receives checkout.session.completed and matches metadata.orderId — and the UPDATE is guarded by `AND status = 'pending'`.

So an order stuck at Pending means one of:
1. The buyer abandoned or failed the Stripe page. Stripe's cancel_url returns them to /marketplace/orders/<id>?payment=cancelled — but the Orders page never reads the `payment` query param, so they get no message either way and often think it worked.
2. The webhook never reached this server (no public URL, wrong endpoint, or STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET set but signature mismatch → 400 "Webhook verification failed: …").
3. Session creation itself failed: the API responds `{ ok: true, order, stripeError }` and the client, which only looks for `stripeSessionUrl`, silently lands the buyer on the order page with a pending order. Look for `marketplace.stripe_error` in the log.

Verify with GET /api/marketplace/stripe/status ({configured:true|false}) before diagnosing anything else. There is no in-app way to re-drive payment for an existing order — cancel it and have the buyer check out again.
symptoms: Buyer paid but status didn't change
No confirmation after returning from Stripe
rootCause: initialStatus = stripe ? 'pending' : 'paid'. Without Stripe the order is fabricated as paid with no charge; with Stripe the only path to 'paid' is the checkout.session.completed webhook, and both a cancelled session and a failed session-creation leave the order pending with no user-visible message because MarketplaceOrdersPage ignores ?payment=.

question: INTERNAL: A seller says their listing went "sold" but no payment ever came through, or a cancelled order never put the stock back.
answer:
Stock is decremented at order CREATION, before any payment is confirmed, and nothing ever reverses it.

What POST /api/marketplace/orders does, in order: creates the order row, then either marks the listing 'sold' (when the ordered quantity meets or exceeds the listing quantity) or decrements marketplace_listings.quantity. This happens whether the order is 'pending' (Stripe) or 'paid' (no Stripe). Consequences to expect on tickets:

1. Abandoned Stripe checkout → order pending forever AND the listing already reads sold / short. The seller sees a phantom sale.
2. Cancelling the order (PATCH … status:'cancelled') only writes marketplace_orders.status and cancelled_by. It does not restore quantity and does not set the listing back to active.
3. Remedy for the seller is manual: My listings → Relist (PATCH status:'active'). That restores visibility but NOT the decremented quantity — if they had 5 and one was taken, they must edit the quantity back, and the Edit button is currently broken, so in practice they delete and re-post.

Also note two disabled guards on this endpoint:
• The "cannot buy your own listing" check is commented out with "TODO: re-enable before production", so a user can order from themselves. The Buy now button is also rendered on your own card in Browse (the isMine check exists only inside the detail modal), which makes accidental self-orders easy.
• Quantity is clamped to the listing quantity server-side, so over-ordering is not possible.

Never describe the phantom-sold state to a customer as a payment problem — it is an inventory bookkeeping gap.

Cancelled order didn't restore the listing

rootCause: Order creation mutates the listing (status='sold' or quantity - qty) unconditionally and no code path ever reverses it; the self-purchase guard is commented out; ListingCard's canBuy does not consider listing.isMine.

question: INTERNAL: An admin says "Connect eBay" (or Connect Amazon) just goes to a broken page even though the API keys are set.
answer:
This is a client bug, not a credentials problem. Confirm the keys first, then explain the workaround.

1. Check GET /api/marketplace/partner-accounts/ebay/status (or …/amazon/status). If it returns configured:false the Connect button would be disabled with "API keys not configured on this server" — that is the credentials case, fix the .env (EBAY_APP_ID / EBAY_CERT_ID / EBAY_REDIRECT_URI, or AMAZON_SP_CLIENT_ID / AMAZON_SP_CLIENT_SECRET / AMAZON_REDIRECT_URI) and restart.
2. If it returns configured:true, the button is enabled and the page calls …/auth-url, which responds `{ ok: true, url }`. The page then does `window.location.href = data.authUrl` — a field the API never sends — so the browser navigates to the literal string "undefined" relative to the current path. The user sees a not-found / blank page and never reaches the consent screen.
3. There is no in-app workaround for the OAuth path. The row can still be created by POSTing to /api/marketplace/partner-accounts with `{platform:'ebay'}`, but that only stores a stub account id — it grants no eBay access.
4. The OAuth callbacks themselves are implemented and, on failure, redirect to /marketplace/partners?error=ebay_auth_failed (or amazon_auth_failed) — the Partners page does not read that param either, so a failed exchange also shows nothing.

Even once connected, neither eBay nor Amazon cross-posts anything: no code publishes a RackTrack listing to either platform. Do not promise cross-posting to customers.

question: INTERNAL: A customer reported a listing and nothing happened. How does reporting and moderation work?
answer:
Reporting works; acting on reports effectively does not. Handle these tickets manually.

What the customer did: opened a listing they don't own, tapped "Report listing", typed a reason and pressed "Submit report". They then saw "Reported. An admin will review this listing." That inserts a row in marketplace_flags. A second report on the same listing from the same account is refused with "already flagged" shown in the modal.

What does not exist:
1. There is no endpoint that lists flags — nothing in the product surfaces reported listings to anyone. The only way to see them is querying marketplace_flags in server/data/auth.db directly.
2. There is no notification of any kind on a flag (unlike listing creation, which fires the Discord webhook).
3. POST /api/marketplace/listings/:id/moderate exists (action 'hide' → status 'closed', 'restore' → 'active') but its own check is `user.role === 'admin' || user.id === 1`. RackTrack has no 'admin' role — the roles are owner, org_admin, site_manager and member — so in practice only the very first user row can moderate; every other account, including the platform owner, gets 403 "admin only".

So the operational answer: escalate to whoever holds user id 1 on that deployment, or have the listing's own seller delete it (DELETE /api/marketplace/listings/:id is owner-only and always available to them). Never tell a customer a review is in progress — nobody is queued to see it.
